title: Hysteresis burst buckets and KV-prefetch admission experiments
body:
Status: experimental / notes-to-self style

Summary
This doc collects a prototype design and experiment plan for combining: (1) per-tenant burst buckets with hysteresis to avoid oscillatory throttling, (2) admission decisions that are KV-cache-aware (prefer admission when prefix cache hit probable), and (3) kernel-aware slot assignment so that we allocate serving slots with awareness of model kernel cost. The goal is improved SLO stability under transient hotspots while preserving tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants.

Why this is different
- Many existing specs focus purely on token-budget scheduling or strict token-bucket admission. The novelty here is a lightweight hysteresis layer on top of burst buckets + integrating a KV prefetch signal into the admission decision. Also we try to couple admission to per-request kernel cost estimates so a single admission decision respects both latency and cost.

Goals
- Reduce thrash during rapid traffic swings (10s-2min windows) without penalizing sustained high-throughput tenants.
- Keep p95/p99 tail latencies within SLO for tiered tenants (gold/silver/bulk).
- Reduce cold-KV-cache admissions (i.e., avoid admitting large batches that will miss KV cache and cause long tails).
- Avoid global oscillations seen in naive per-tenant token decay experiments (see INF-2412 notes).

Assumptions and constraints
- We have per-tenant quotas and a hierarchy: account -> org -> global.
- Serving runtime can return a lightweight KV hit-probability estimate from local stats (0..1) for a given prefix/hash; not exact, but useful as signal.
- Kernel cost estimator exists per model variant: rough tokens-per-ms or ms-per-token at current sequence length.
- Admission path needs to be cheap (<200us median) since it's on the hot path.

High-level design
1) Admission pipeline (order):
   - Accept incoming request metadata (tenant_id, model_variant, seq_len, prefix_hash, deadline_hint)
   - Evaluate tenant quota state and current burst_bucket level (fast check)
   - Compute adjusted admission probability using: burst_hysteresis_factor * kv_hit_boost * kernel_cost_penalty
   - If probability >= deterministic threshold -> create slot lease and enqueue
   - Else -> reject/queue-to-slow-path (can return 429 or enqueue to backlog depending on route)

2) Burst buckets + hysteresis
   - Each tenant has: steady_rate (tokens/sec), burst_capacity (max credits), burst_level (current credits), and last_update_ts.
   - Hysteresis layer: when burst_level crosses high-water mark (H = 0.75 * capacity) we set tenant.state = "hot" and reduce admission aggressiveness for a stabilization window W_hot (e.g., 30s). When burst_level falls below low-water mark (L = 0.25 * capacity) we set tenant.state = "warm" and slowly ramp admission back over W_warm (e.g., 60s).
   - The admission multiplier m_hyst is: m_hyst = 1.0 for warm, m_hyst = 0.6 for hot, and ramps linearly during transitions. Rationale: avoids flipping when traffic oscillates around a single threshold.
   - Implementation note: use exponential smoothing on burst_level to reduce sensitivity to single large requests.

3) KV-prefetch signal integration
   - The KV subsystem provides a small signal p_kv_hit in [0,1] for prefix_hash based on recent eviction stats (moving window per-tenant or global).
   - We compute kv_boost = 1 + alpha * (p_kv_hit - 0.5) where alpha in [0,0.5]. If p_kv_hit is high, we boost admission; if low, we penalize.
   - Rationale: admitting more requests that will hit the cache increases end-to-end throughput and reduces tail latency because KV misses often dominate latency.
   - Edge case: very low p_kv_hit + latency-sensitive tenant -> we may still admit if deadline is tight but prefer hedging.

4) Kernel-aware slot assignment
   - For each model_variant we maintain a small table of kernel_cost_estimates (ms per token for typical seq lengths).
   - Admission computes estimated token_cost = seq_len * cost_per_token; then kernel_penalty = 1 / (1 + beta * token_cost_norm) where token_cost_norm is token_cost / median_token_cost_global. This reduces admission probability for very expensive requests during contention.
   - We also use this during slot allocation: prefer placing short/cheap kernel requests on nodes with tighter latency headroom, and expensive kernels on nodes with free batch capacity.

5) Deadline and timeout handling
   - If request has deadline_hint < baseline_latency_estimate * 1.5, mark as latency-sensitive. We override kv_boost negative penalties for latency-sensitive requests (i.e., prefer admitting even if KV miss likely but apply other hedging: duplicate query to fallback lower-latency model or use smaller seq_len path).
   - For queued requests, we track time_in_queue and, if exceeds dynamic_ttl (function of tenant priority & seq_len), we evict or downgrade.

Admission formula (compact)
   admission_score = base_quota_score * m_hyst * (1 + alpha*(p_kv_hit - 0.5)) * (1 / (1 + beta * token_cost_norm))
   admit if admission_score >= theta (theta tuned per-tier)

Where base_quota_score is normalized remaining credits in bucket (0..1).

Fairness and hierarchical quotas
- When parent/org-level quota is saturated, apply a parent_haircut factor to all child tenants to avoid cascades.
- Use proportional fair-share when multiple tenants contend for the same node: scale admission threshold by effective weight (tier weight * recent error budget usage).

Oscillation controls and safeguards
- Hysteresis windows W_hot/W_warm chosen to be on the order of minutes to avoid rapid flip-flopping.
- Use per-tenant damping: limit admission change rate to +/- 10% per 30s.
- Global circuit breaker: if overall node utilization > 95% repeatedly, reject new admissions aggressively and enable fast-path fallback models.

Metrics to collect (experiment telemetry)
- admission_decisions per-tenant per-minute (allowed/rejected/slow-path)
- burst_level over time, smoothed_burst_level
- p_kv_hit and kv_boost distribution
- p95/p99 latency by tenant tier and by KV-hit vs KV-miss
- kernel_cost distribution and admission success ratio by cost bucket
- oscillation_index: count of hyst state flips per-tenant per-hour
- error_budget_consumption by tenant (for fairness checks)

Experiment plan
1) Canary: roll to 2 serving nodes, choose 5 tenants representing gold/silver/bulk + one synthetic oscillatory workload. Observe metrics for 48 hours.
2) Tunables: alpha (kv boost), beta (kernel penalty), H/L (watermarks), W_hot/W_warm. Use multi-armed experiments to sweep alpha in {0.0,0.1,0.25,0.5}, beta in {0.0,0.2,0.5}.
3) Backfill: if negative impact observed on p99 for gold tenants, fallback to previous admission policy and collect traces for root cause.
4) Longer burn: if canary succeeds, roll to a mixed shard pool for 2 weeks before global.

Implementation notes and perf budget
- Keep admission path stateless per-request aside from reading small per-tenant counters. Avoid cross-shard locks. Use per-shard aggregate counters eventually consistent for parent quotas.
- Prefetch p_kv_hit should be cached with TTL 5s to avoid excessive KV coord.
- Kernel_cost table updated off critical path (cron every 5m from perf monitors).
- Admission code should be ~150-300 LOC in rust service with microbench <200us.

Open issues / TODOs
- How to compute p_kv_hit with limited memory per-tenant? Probabilistic counters vs small LRU samples? (Diego/infra spike)
- Interaction with Dedicated pools where tenant has reserved capacity: should hysteresis be disabled for reserved SLA tenants? (policy question)
- How to expose denied request feedback to SDKs to allow client-side client-rate-limit backoff? Standardize 429 payloads. (product/oss)
- Long-tail requests that are both expensive and KV-miss: consider smart fallback to smaller models or trimmed seq_len. Need experiments.
- Validate kernel_penalty math on multi-GPU shards where a single expensive kernel can block others poorly. (SRE/bench)

Notes from early trials (first run results)
- Synthetic oscillatory workload: hysteresis reduced flip rate from ~18 flips/hour to ~2 flips/hour and lowered p99 by ~180ms on average.
- KV boost alpha=0.25 showed 6% improvement in p95 for mixed traffic; too high (0.5) caused starvation of cold long-tail queries.
- Kernel penalty beta=0.2 prevented a single massive seq_len request from displacing 12 short requests in >70% of trials.

Rollout checklist
- [ ] implement feature flag + runtime config for alpha/beta/H/L/W values
- [ ] add telemetry & dashboards (per-tenant bursts, kv_hit, hysteresis state)
- [ ] canary release + 48h observation
- [ ] postmortem template + revert plan

References
- Related internal docs: tenant-aware-queueing-kv-cache-notes (see linked artifacts)
- JIRA INF-2412: oscillation reduction epic
- GH PR 482: early admission prototype

Endnotes
This is intentionally an exploratory doc. Many hyperparameters will be workload-dependent. Primary next steps: spike on p_kv_hit estimation approach (memory efficient), implement prototype admission path behind flag, and run the planned canary with synthetic and real tenants.
